Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

feedback.scope: Mineral & Walnut first-floor architecture audit and entry/office/media refinements
feedback.userFeedback: Audit every first-floor day and night image against original model-home photographs, the blueprint and actual-house evidence. Office: move the gallery doorway toward the right in the reverse view, retain the small circular window to its left, and place the printer cabinet and artwork on the larger left wall section. Both exterior window banks are centered paired 2×2 assemblies, not three-unit windows. Media: smaller centered square-looking 2×2 main window; RH Cloud sofa with ottomans extending both ends, small side tables and a central table; 83-inch TV and a wider console built into a redesigned TV-wall composition. Homeowner confirms the smaller media seating-wall exterior feature is a fake window with no inside opening. Entry arch wording becomes “Welcome Home”; departing wording becomes “See you next time.”
feedback.interpretation: Record a fresh first-floor correction pass in pure Mineral & Walnut. Existing thin glazing bars were incorrectly described as three structural window units; do not propagate that error. Keep media seating wall solid in every angle, despite the brochure symbol. Retain light clear side doors, two-story cascade chandelier, neutral oak/ivory/mushroom/walnut palette, selected stone updates and uncovered stairs. New renders remain pending until source-by-source visual QA; the gym is retained and the plan-led bathroom access offsets are checked.

schedule.item: Ivory sheers + hidden privacy shades; no mandatory blackout

schedule.dimensions: Site-measured opening and track sizes, finished drop, returns and operating clearances. No quantities or fabrication dimensions inferred from render pixels.
schedule.procurement: Manual system allowance: goods $850–$1500 before tax/delivery; direct installation $200–$350 before GC markup. Already included in the Option 1 cost plan. Exact material, lining, track and finished coverage to be selected.

feedback.userFeedback: Return entrance gallery to light doors; dark doors take too much attention. Office: entire north wall built out; large desk facing northwest instead of semicircle. Media: follow supplied vertical wood-slat TV-wall reference in our style; M2 door must be on west wall per blueprint. Gym: empty finished room with walls, mirror, selected quote and floor; owner will add equipment later. Start floor two.
feedback.interpretation: Warm ivory glazed side-door leaves replace charcoal on both room and gallery faces. Rectangular walnut office desk with southeast task chair facing northwest and full north-wall cabinetry replaces the curved desk and compact bookcase; south console remains omitted. Media south TV wall becomes walnut slats with long charcoal-front walnut console, subtle TV backlight and under-console light; west entry opening remains on perpendicular wall. Gym equipment, storage furniture and decor are deferred; retain northwest closet and separate bath access. Begin five photographed second-floor spaces with consistent finishes.

feedback.scope: floors 1–3 refinements, missing living room and all-bedroom flooring
feedback.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

feedback.scope: first floor revisions and start of second floor
feedback.userFeedback: Return entrance gallery to light doors; dark doors take too much attention. Office: entire north wall built out; large desk facing northwest instead of semicircle. Media: follow supplied vertical wood-slat TV-wall reference in our style; M2 door must be on west wall per blueprint. Gym: empty finished room with walls, mirror, selected quote and floor; owner will add equipment later. Start floor two.
feedback.interpretation: Warm ivory glazed side-door leaves replace charcoal on both room and gallery faces. Rectangular walnut office desk with southeast task chair facing northwest and full north-wall cabinetry replaces the curved desk and compact bookcase; south console remains omitted. Media south TV wall becomes walnut slats with long charcoal-front walnut console, subtle TV backlight and under-console light; west entry opening remains on perpendicular wall. Gym equipment, storage furniture and decor are deferred; retain northwest closet and separate bath access. Begin five photographed second-floor spaces with consistent finishes.
feedback.resultingRevision: first-floor review r03; second-floor review r01

feedback.scope: floors 1–3 refinements, missing living room and all-bedroom flooring
feedback.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

dining.designIntent: Warm formal dining with a walnut extension table for eight daily and up to ten after measured fit, sculptural pendant, console and neutral artwork. Dining opens directly to the piano salon; real east/south windows and the shared small high arch retain their source relationships.

sourceEvidence.confidence: Real model-home architecture; finishes are not the homeowner-selected scheme
observations: Original camera: image-left is the continuous east facade with the nearer smaller high-sill arch and two tall rectangular/transom windows; ahead are two tall south-wall arches; image-right is the west console/art wall.

The oblique thin arch at photo-right does not establish a closed niche. The plan establishes a butler-pantry passage on this interior wall; preserve the passage and confirm its exact visible detail on site.
Living connects directly beyond the original camera across the north boundary. Retain a continuous floor and flat ceiling; no artificial portal/header is supported.

sourceEvidence.confidence: Builder plan, not measured as-built
observations: Plan room label 12 ft 11 in × 15 ft 3 in at printed-plan bottom/left. Printed top=west, right=north, bottom=east and left=south; nominal plan relationships are not an as-built survey.
The printed-plan top/west console wall backs the entry-gallery open-to-below void and contains the real butler-pantry arched passage toward its south end.

The north/printed-right dining edge is directly open to living without a drawn partition or framed portal. The straight common east facade retains the smaller high arch near the zone junction, with tall dining and living windows on either side.

architectureLocks: Preserve the original photo openings: two east-facade tall rectangles with shallow transoms, one smaller HIGH-SILL arch near the living junction on that SAME straight facade, and two south-facade tall arched windows. Preserve original head/sill/trim relationships; these are not five identical openings.

Printed-plan top=west: the console/art wall backs the entry-gallery open-to-below void. Keep the sideboard here and preserve the real butler-pantry arched passage toward the printed-plan left/south end. The oblique thin arched photo feature does not prove a closed wall niche.

Printed-plan right=north: dining directly connects to living across an open seam with continuous oak floor and flat ceiling. Do not add a partition, portal, pier, jamb, arch or dropped header. The central small arch remains once on the shared east facade, not on a perpendicular invented corner.
Plan label 12 ft 11 in × 15 ft 3 in; field verification governs.
Closed extension table target 84 × 40 in for eight: three chairs per long side and one at each end. About 108 in extended for occasional ten, subject to the actual table supports and chair plan.

Nominal centered closed-table end gaps 49.5 in and side gaps 57.5 in before chairs, trim or storage. Extended end gaps reduce to 37.5 in. These are planning arithmetic, not verified usable clearances.
A square twelve-seat table is not proposed; preserve circulation.
Shallow walnut shelf beneath the high arch, concept about 8 in deep, without covering glazing.

feedback.scope: first floor revisions and start of second floor
feedback.userFeedback: Return entrance gallery to light doors; dark doors take too much attention. Office: entire north wall built out; large desk facing northwest instead of semicircle. Media: follow supplied vertical wood-slat TV-wall reference in our style; M2 door must be on west wall per blueprint. Gym: empty finished room with walls, mirror, selected quote and floor; owner will add equipment later. Start floor two.
feedback.interpretation: Warm ivory glazed side-door leaves replace charcoal on both room and gallery faces. Rectangular walnut office desk with southeast task chair facing northwest and full north-wall cabinetry replaces the curved desk and compact bookcase; south console remains omitted. Media south TV wall becomes walnut slats with long charcoal-front walnut console, subtle TV backlight and under-console light; west entry opening remains on perpendicular wall. Gym equipment, storage furniture and decor are deferred; retain northwest closet and separate bath access. Begin five photographed second-floor spaces with consistent finishes.

feedback.scope: floors 1–3 refinements, missing living room and all-bedroom flooring
feedback.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

feedback.scope: floors 1–3 refinements, missing living room and all-bedroom flooring
feedback.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

feedback.userFeedback: Entry: match second-floor wood color. Office: TV and soundbar in north cabinetry, artwork and small printer cabinet right of entry door. Media: clear entry doors, collectible shelves right of doors, less intense TV wall, soundbar, ceiling and behind-sofa speakers. Great room: sibling artworks above both consoles. Kitchen: better island lights. Dining: explore larger table for ten versus square twelve, fill space below high window. Living room: baby grand, Cloud couch, sheer drapes, two blueprint-derived angles. Sunroom: rectangular six-seat table, better chandelier, sheer drapes. All bedrooms: hard floors with loose rug under beds. Owner bedroom: 55-inch TV and soundbar instead of dresser art, art above bed, platform and bedside underside LEDs. Owner bath: artwork above tub. Bedroom 2: correct bed/desk/door layout; clarified headboard WEST and entry at southern WEST wall, desk right of EAST window. Laundry: graphic and exact wording “Rinse and repeat..”. Clarified oak/rug applies to penthouse bedroom too.
feedback.interpretation: Preserve the individual bedroom identities and common warm modern palette. Propose rectangular 108 × 42 in dining table for ten, subject to actual circulation survey. Use plan-informed living room and explicitly record Bedroom 2 closet/door conflict rather than claiming its new layout is surveyed. All new images are proposals; measurements, products and trade details remain unselected.

guide.title: A home that feels considered.
guide.subtitle: Mineral & Walnut, refined around your life.
guide.position: Warm ivory and mushroom, rich walnut, natural oak and neutral textiles define Mineral & Walnut. Selected warm stone enriches the kitchen and bathrooms. Bedrooms retain their original individual designs; exposed wood stairs connect the floors.
guide.scope: MW-NR01: 24 spaces, 45 day views and 24 night views. Neutral bedrooms restored and exposed wood stairs coordinated across day/night; A/C1/E stone updates retained.

rules.title: Start with the room’s job
rules.text: Plan the walk, the seat, the light and the place to put a drink before choosing decoration. Write down the daily routine and the storage it needs.

rules.title: Give each view a hierarchy
rules.text: Choose a lead element, then supporting elements. Your TV and fireplace can read as one composition. A room can have several functional zones without every wall becoming a feature.

rules.title: Keep the materials related
rules.text: Natural oak floors, warm mineral/ivory walls, rich walnut and restrained black accents carry across the house. Repeat these materials with different proportions and silhouettes in each room.

rules.title: Vary the silhouettes
rules.text: Balance soft upholstery, rounded tables and substantial walnut storage. Use legs, plinths or floating details according to the room and practical construction needs.

rules.title: Design for daylight and evening
rules.text: Test material boards near several windows and under the intended lamps. Use sheers for softness, a separate privacy or blackout layer where needed, and controllable task and accent light.

rules.title: Leave something unfilled
rules.text: Empty wall and clear surfaces give art and architecture room to matter. Collectibles, family photos and seasonal decor belong in intentional groups, with storage for the rest.

materials.title: Walls: quiet mineral character
materials.use: Propose Roman Clay on selected dry focal surfaces, with washable warm matte paint elsewhere. Keep the application smooth and subtle in this sunlit house.
materials.detail: Price surface preparation separately. Compare a real sample of each finish with the same floor, upholstery and trim; the render does not specify a paint color.

materials.title: Limewash: an alternative finish
materials.use: Use when a softer brushed, cloudy surface is wanted. It is not an automatic protective layer over decorative paint.
materials.detail: Follow the selected system’s primer and sealer instructions. A wipeable surface is not a waterproof splash assembly; use appropriate tile/stone and substrate systems at wet zones.

materials.title: Floors: continuity with purpose
materials.use: Budget replacement natural oak in connected dry spaces and all four bedrooms, with separate rugs. Keep a single coordinated undertone through circulation and adjacent rooms.
materials.detail: Wet bathrooms, laundry needs and the gym may need different appropriate materials. Check substrate, moisture, stair levels and thresholds. Wide planks alone do not make a floor better.

materials.title: Walnut + dark accents
materials.use: Use rich walnut for selected cabinetry, consoles and the owner-suite headwall. Natural oak flooring keeps the backdrop lighter; restrained black frames and hardware provide definition.
materials.detail: Approve a shared walnut sample. Grain, veneer sequencing, edge details and hardware quality matter more than repeating the same furniture shape everywhere.

materials.title: Drapery: daylight and privacy
materials.use: Sleeping and cinema spaces: sheers plus blackout. Social rooms: sheers plus a discreet privacy shade. Working/wet areas: practical shades. See the complete 24-space schedule below.
materials.detail: Keep ivory/oatmeal textile faces and slim dark or concealed hardware. Sheers alone are used only where privacy and light-control needs are verified absent. Full closing coverage, returns and stack-back matter more than decorative side panels.

materials.title: Light: layered, quiet and serviceable
materials.use: Design target: 2700K in relaxed spaces and coordinated 3000K task areas, or compatible warm-dim systems; judge connected sightlines as a whole.
materials.detail: Aim for 90+ CRI, but also check glare, output, dimmer compatibility and flicker. Mock up the actual fixture and control. Keep LED drivers accessible and dots out of view.

materials.title: Selected stone-look porcelain · A / C1 / E
materials.use: A: pearl onyx appearance around the primary bathing areas. C1: cream quartzite appearance on kitchen worktops, backsplash and waterfall. E: pale limestone appearance behind the shared vanity and on the doorway return. Original mineral fireplace retained while its choice remains open.
materials.detail: These are porcelain appearance directions, not selected natural stone or product SKUs. Confirm physical samples, approved applications, format, layout, joints, edges and installation with the relevant fabricator. Obtain the actual cost difference before committing to the finishes.

qualifications: “Go bigger”
Choose the largest piece that still fits circulation, doors, reach and daily use. Our dining table needs a plan test before any increase.
“One focal point”
Use a clear visual hierarchy within each view or zone; a fireplace and TV can be one composition. Keep the existing TV location unless separately redesigned.
“Never mix color temperatures”
Avoid accidental mismatches within a scene. Deliberate warm-dim lamps or task layers can coexist when tested together.
“Paint is two shades darker on a full wall”
There is no reliable fixed two-shade conversion. Test large physical samples across daylight and evening conditions.
“50% strength means half as dark”
A tint formula change is not a predictable lightness conversion. Select and sample the actual proposed color.
“Satin everywhere wet; flat everywhere dry”
Choose an actual coating system for cleaning, moisture and substrate. Sheen alone does not establish durability or waterproofing.
“One antique / three repeats / 60–30–10”
Useful prompts, not quotas. Personal pieces and visual balance matter more than counting objects or percentages.
“Buy custom for a luxury result”
Custom solves a specific fit or storage problem. Use well-made retail furniture; quote stock boxes with tailored fronts where appropriate. No guaranteed saving percentage.
“Replace all ordinary finishes”
Spend where an upgrade changes comfort, function or a key view. Retention, refinishing and good installation can be the better choice.
“TV distance is a fixed diagonal multiple”
Use the chosen screen, resolution, content, viewing preference and actual seat location. Test at full size; the playbook’s multiplier is not universal.
measurements: Main circulation
Start around 36 in clear; aim for more on busy routes
Planning target, not an accessibility or code approval; include open doors and drawer positions.
Kitchen work aisles
42 in for one cook / 48 in for multiple cooks
NKBA design recommendations; measure counter/appliance fronts. Accessible layouts and local requirements may need more.
Dining circulation
Aim for 42–48 in where people pass behind seats
Check the real pulled-out chair and cabinet projection. Table-to-wall arithmetic alone is not a usable aisle.
Sofa to coffee table
Start around 14–18 in
Adjust to seat depth, knee room, reach and mobility. Do not sacrifice the main route.
Artwork
Start near 57–60 in center on an open wall
Artwork over furniture relates to the furniture and architecture; mock it up rather than forcing eye-level rules.
Rug sizing
Keep the seating group connected; allow dining chairs to stay on the rug
Use actual furniture footprints. A larger rug cannot correct an oversized table.
Bedside use
Start with 30–36 in comfortable circulation where feasible
Coordinate with bed drawers, door swings and the user’s access needs; measure nightstands against the actual mattress.
Pendents + chandeliers
Use the table/island, fixture scale and sightline
The room-length-plus-width formula is only a sketch; actual fixture instructions and clearance requirements govern.

phases.title: 01 · Resolve and sample
phases.text: Measure the house, tape furniture layouts and approve a shared material board. Resolve Bedroom 5 construction, Bedroom 2 geometry, dining clearances and nighttime privacy.
phases.spend: Pay for the survey, drawings and real samples before committing to fabrication.

phases.title: 02 · Coordinate fixed work
phases.text: Assume most finishes need replacement. Coordinate Bedroom 5 partitions, flooring, wet-room systems, electrical changes and useful walnut built-ins. Retain service locations where feasible.
phases.spend: Quote prep, materials, installation, disposal and tax separately; compare retention and replacement where realistic.

phases.title: 03 · Build the comfort layer
phases.text: Buy new furniture against an agreed schedule: beds and mattresses, seating, rugs, drapery and useful tables. Furnish the primary living and sleeping rooms first.
phases.spend: Prioritize touch points and daily comfort. Keep a contingency appropriate to the surveyed scope rather than a universal furnishing percentage.

phases.title: 04 · Collect and adjust
phases.text: Add art, plants and seasonal decoration once the core rooms work. Later purchases may be phased; they are deferred costs, not permanent savings.
phases.spend: Use movable accents for experiments. Avoid a whole-house replacement order before the first rooms work.

checks: measure
Measured plans include doors, windows, services and delivery routes.
furniture
New furniture is measured, budgeted and allocated by room before ordering.
sample
Wall, floor, wood, metal and textile samples reviewed together in daylight and evening light.
layout
Furniture taped out; doors, drawers and chairs operate without blocking key routes.
privacy
Sheer, privacy and blackout needs tested after dark.
light
Lighting layers, control compatibility, glare and service access checked.
joinery
Joinery drawings show hardware, hinges, supports, power and ventilation.
wet
Wet-zone materials and waterproofing system coordinated with installer.
budget
Quotes separate materials, prep and labor; quantities, lead times and contingency are recorded.
handoff
Finish/product schedule, sample references, drawings and open questions issued together.
guide.seasonal: Keep the permanent background calm. Christmas can bring evergreen, deep red, silver or warm lights; Halloween can use charcoal, amber and branches. Rotate a few textiles and objects, retain clear walkways, and reserve a storage location for each seasonal set. No permanent yellow/blue requirement.

priorities.title: Resolve the furniture plan
priorities.text: Formal dining, sunroom, piano salon, media seating and Bedroom 2 are the highest fit risks. Full-size furniture footprints and opening clearances come before another styling pass.

priorities.title: Complete the missing spaces
priorities.text: The main-level powder room, walk-in pantry, menu center, butler’s pantry and main-level terrace need explicit design decisions. Their existence and exact configuration must be checked against this house. Powder/pantry remodels are expressly excluded from the current base estimate beyond shared dry-area paint.

priorities.title: Make the render set tell one consistent story
priorities.text: The revised set coordinates oak bedroom floors, media finishes and glazing, room-specific window layers and day/night furnishings. Source views and derived concepts are labeled; confirm unseen junctions and dimensions on site.

priorities.title: Make lighting useful and controllable
priorities.text: Separate arrival, conversation, movie, reading, task and cleaning scenes. The salon needs a lower light layer, media art lights should dim/off for films, and suite LEDs should not dominate every evening scene. Choose actual dimmable products and test them; rendered orange/pink color casts do not identify a lamp or paint color.

priorities.title: Give the rooms personal identity
priorities.text: Keep the neutral palette and greenery. Replace some repeated beige abstract pairs with personally meaningful photography, a single larger artwork, textile art or a sculptural object. Retain the requested sibling artwork in the great room and bed art. Give dining and sunroom distinct pendant silhouettes.

priorities.title: Finish everyday comfort and storage
priorities.text: Plan where keys, bags, shoes, drinks, chargers, luggage, towels, toiletries, laundry, cleaning tools and seasonal decorations live. Much is mentioned in allowances but not located or dimensioned. Test actual seat and mattress comfort; hide cables and allow service access.

priorities.title: Spend on finish quality where it shows
priorities.text: Use one natural-oak sample, one coordinated walnut stain family and a small controlled paint/trim palette. Use specialty mineral finish selectively, quality washable coatings elsewhere, and appropriate wet-area finishes. Refine installation and proportion before commissioning more wall panels or bespoke cabinetry.

fitChecks.text: Formal dining plan zone 155 × 183 in. Revised closed table target 84 × 40 in gives nominal centered end gaps of 49.5 in and side gaps of 57.5 in before chairs, trim or storage. A 108-in extended table reduces end gaps to 37.5 in. These are planning arithmetic, not verified usable clearance; test all chairs and supports before ordering.

Plan zone 147 × 111 in; proposed table 72 × 34 in. Centered nominal gaps are 37.5 in at ends and 38.5 in at sides before chair pullback, drape stacks and obstructions. Check the nearby oven and terrace-door operation with all seats in use.

The printed living-room zone is 16 ft × 11 ft 4 in. A roughly 5-ft piano and 96-in sofa are only concepts. Verify the selected piano case, open lid, bench travel and delivery route with actual seating footprints.

rooms.action: Retain windowless compact shell, vanity/toilet opposite shower and existing B2 right-hand bench. Verify staggered studio-near-vanity versus hall-near-shower doors, handing and simultaneous privacy. Retain practical accessory/storage and compatible waterproofing/ventilation requirements.
rooms.previousFinding: Towel/robe storage and accessory positions are underdeveloped; the plan-led geometry is not surveyed.
rooms.rendered: Published prior images remain; the corrections below are instructions, not a statement that new renders have passed QA.
rooms.priorRenderAssessment: Ivory porcelain floor restored; vanity/toilet end, two side accesses and windowless plan retained. Reverse windowless Bath 3 view shows shower opposite vanity/toilet, with side access doors and coordinated porcelain.

rooms.title: Great room
rooms.keep: This is one of the strongest rooms: ivory seating, walnut storage, sibling art and the fireplace form a coherent composition.
rooms.finding: GR1/GR2 broadly retain source architecture; restore real terrace mullions/transom proportions and make furnishings less repetitive, maintain sibling artworks.
rooms.action: Keep the sibling-art requirement. Add a reachable drink table at the lounge chair if the measured layout permits; choose actual comfortable upholstery and a distinctive textile weave. Test TV height full-size from the selected sofa. Avoid adding another feature wall.
rooms.previousFinding: The above-fireplace TV needs a seated-height and product-clearance check. Tables and art are attractive but repeat the same formula used elsewhere.
rooms.rendered: Two high transoms and terrace glazing retained; sibling art, seating and reachable drink table coordinated. Companion great-room camera retains transoms, terrace glazing, sibling artworks and furnishing layout.

rooms.title: Kitchen
rooms.keep: The retained service layout, dark dome pendants and walnut island belong to the palette.
rooms.finding: K2 relocated refrigerator to long cooktop run; work aisle/reverse architecture wrong. K1 warm cast and busy counter. Coordinate sunroom sightline.
rooms.action: Sample a quieter pale counter and warm-ivory cabinet finish, with simple door profiles if replacing cabinets. Coordinate backsplash and counters. Verify island seating, landing surfaces, ventilation, appliance cut sheets and task-light glare. Correct image white balance before judging paint undertones.
rooms.previousFinding: The counter looks busier than the calm stone language elsewhere; gray cabinet color and orange/pink image casts weaken consistency. Four stools and appliance-door clearances have not been measured.
rooms.rendered: Original refrigerator return, cooktop, window and oven column retained; cabinetry warmed, four stools and sunroom retained. Physical counter sample governs subtle veining. Actual reverse kitchen photo anchors refrigerator return, work aisle, sink/DW and archways; finish and dome pendants match K1.

rooms.title: Formal dining
rooms.keep: The rectangular table and daylight are right for this house.
rooms.finding: D1 window heights distorted, ten-seat fixed-table clearance unresolved. D2 small arch enlarged and rendered without reference room context.

Keep the requested feature below the high window shallow and useful. Choose a more substantial sculptural dining light, distinct from the airy sunroom fixture.
rooms.previousFinding: The 108 × 42-inch ten-seat concept is tight at the ends after cabinets. The small open shelf creates another display area; the chandelier closely repeats the sunroom.
rooms.rendered: Five photographed opening locations and high arch retained; eight-seat closed extension table, shallow shelf and differentiated pendant shown. Useful high-window/shelf detail preserves small high arch and adjacent tall windows without enlarging opening.

rooms.title: Living room · piano salon
rooms.keep: The piano gives this room a distinct identity and should remain the main feature.
rooms.finding: No dedicated room photo; prior views imply new partitions/portal and an unverified window/transom arrangement. Plan is open to dining; piano footprint must be honest.
rooms.action: Template the exact piano, open lid, bench withdrawal, sofa and chair together. Add one good reading lamp and a reachable small table. Keep artwork singular and expressive. Confirm piano delivery and location against direct sun/air supply using the selected maker’s guidance.
rooms.previousFinding: The 16 ft × 11 ft 4 in plan zone must accommodate a real piano, bench and sofa. The night view relies mainly on ceiling lights; paired views do not verify delivery or bench space.
rooms.rendered: Plan-led living study now shows open dining boundary, two front living windows, solid east-side wall, compact piano/sofa/chair arrangement and no invented portal. Tighter framing excludes unsupported ceiling details; no dedicated living photograph exists. Piano-side secondary concept retains two front windows, sofa at the open dining boundary, one chair, walnut table and baby grand. No dedicated room photograph; the apparent header at the dining opening is an unverified junction, not a proposed structural alteration or confirmed existing beam.

rooms.title: Sunroom
rooms.keep: Six-place everyday dining with light sheers is appropriate.
rooms.finding: S1/S2 nearly identical. Original oven/window geometry broadly retained. Match warm ivory kitchen and provide second meaningful source-adjacent view.
rooms.action: Retain six seats with slim, comfortable chairs and a rounded-corner rectangular table. Tape the footprint and move real chairs before ordering. Keep the chandelier visually light, tracks simple and appliance/terrace access clear.
rooms.previousFinding: Nominal 72 × 34-inch furniture in the 147 × 111-inch zone leaves limited space once chairs, curtains and nearby oven/door operation are included. Both images show almost the same angle.
rooms.rendered: Window banks, transoms/knee walls, oven column and terrace door preserved; six-seat table and privacy layers visible. Closer kitchen-side sunroom perspective retains six chairs, wraparound transoms and knee walls, pendant and layers.

rooms.finding: OB1/OB2 shrank four-sash bank into three in some views; bedside LED glare and repeated beige art. Preserve requested suite design.
rooms.action: Give reading, headwall ambience and low-level floor lighting separate controls. Use a subtle glow with no visible diode dots; sleep mode switches decorative LEDs off. Retain artwork over the bed but select a distinctive composition. Prioritize mattress, bedding, reading comfort and bedside charging over extra built-outs.
rooms.previousFinding: The headwall, underbed and bedside LEDs are all visually prominent at once; artwork repeats the paired-neutral formula. Exact bedside heights and reach remain unselected.
rooms.rendered: Original neutral primary suite restored: ivory bedding, oatmeal textiles, charcoal details and walnut. Retain its individual headwall, platform bed and lighting.

rooms.title: Owners retreat
rooms.keep: A quiet coffee and reading nook is a useful complement to the bedroom.

rooms.action: Reconcile the adjoining suite with current oak flooring, loose rugs and the approved bed/headwall. Use a useful tray and restrained coffee setup. Keep blackout coordinated with the open bedroom connection; consider quiet appliance operation when selecting the beverage unit.

rooms.title: Owners walk-in closet

rooms.title: Bedroom 2
rooms.keep: The restrained upholstered bed and desk suit a compact guest/work room.
rooms.finding: Earlier owner-directed concept conflicted with builder-plan closet and entry. Homeowner now says follow blueprint, closet against shared bathroom.

sources.title: Roger Oates — Why wool?
sources.note: Manufacturer describes wool flatweave’s sound absorption and suitability for skilled fitting around curved stairs. No house-specific noise reduction or safety guarantee is claimed.

sources.title: Portola — Roman Clay application and limitations
sources.note: Roman Clay is for smooth interior walls and is not specified by the manufacturer for wet areas such as inside showers. Select the full substrate/finish system for each location.

firstFloorUpdate.status: Requirements updated; replacement first-floor renders and visual QA pending. Existing cost allowances and purchasing decisions are unchanged.

active.priorVerdict: Mineral & Walnut now has a corrected, coordinated 45-day / 24-night review set. The remaining work is measured fit, product and material selection, trade details and the ancillary spaces listed below—not more whole-house decorative features.

firstFloorRevision.status: Visually reviewed proposed design; awaiting homeowner feedback

secondFloorRevision.status: Visually reviewed proposed design; awaiting homeowner feedback

windows.status: Recommended room schedule; exact products and measured quantities pending
windows.summary: Blackout where people sleep or watch movies; sheers with a separate privacy layer in social rooms; compact practical shades in working and wet areas. Sheers alone are reserved for glazing verified to have no privacy or blackout requirement.
windows.palette: Warm ivory linen-look sheers, ivory or oatmeal blackout curtain faces, and quiet warm-neutral shades. Concealed or slim dark tracks coordinate with walnut, natural oak and restrained black details. Blackout describes the backing, not a black visible curtain.
windows.renderNote: MW-A02 corrects visible openings against original photographs and the blueprint. Day shows open layers; night demonstrates privacy/blackout closed where visible. Bedroom 2 follows the clarified stair-hall/closet layout; Bedroom 5 reverse view interprets its planned front windows. Rendered operation is not a tested privacy or blackout result.

rules.title: Sheers soften daylight; privacy is separate
rules.text: Keep the airy sheer appearance in living rooms, but include an independently operated, non-see-through privacy shade behind it. An open-weave solar screen is not a substitute for an evening privacy layer. Test the actual sample from outside with the room lights on; silhouettes can remain visible through some light-filtering fabrics.

rules.title: Blackout requires coverage as well as fabric
rules.text: For dual curtains, place sheers closest to the glass and fully closing blackout-lined panels on an independent room-side track. Resolve center overlap, wall returns and top/bottom light gaps. Where furniture prevents functional curtains, substitute a blackout roller behind the sheers. Fabric alone does not guarantee a completely dark room.

rules.title: When just sheers are enough
rules.text: Only where an after-dark sightline check confirms no privacy need and the room has no sleep or cinema requirement. No occupied bedroom or street-facing social room is assigned sheers alone by default. Verified private high glazing can remain bare; a sheer-only treatment there is an aesthetic choice.

rules.title: Keep the construction simple
rules.text: Base pricing assumes manual tracks and cordless shades, retail or semi-custom fabric, and surface-mounted hardware. No rebuilt ceiling pockets or motors. Measure track width, stack-back, opening operation, furniture and floor variation; choose fullness with the fabricator for the actual heading and fabric. Avoid puddled fabric.

rules.title: Price openings once
rules.text: The room amounts below are provisional allowances, not a window count or supplier quotation. Replace them with a labeled opening-by-opening survey before ordering. Interior glazed doors, transoms and terrace doors must be identified separately; windowless rooms receive no new curtain allowance.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · opacity and privacy
sources.note: Sheers offer little privacy; light-filtering fabrics vary in opacity. Manufacturer guidance informs performance distinctions, not the room design or prices.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · blackout and light gaps
sources.note: Mounting, overlaps, liners and side channels influence room darkening. No particular brand or product is specified.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · bathroom window treatments
sources.note: Consider humidity and window location when selecting material; direct shower exposure needs explicit product suitability.

sources.title: Hunter Douglas · solar shade limitations
sources.note: A solar-screen shade does not reliably provide nighttime privacy when the interior is illuminated.

rooms.recommendation: No gallery drapes; discreet privacy shade on exterior entrance glass if needed
rooms.coverage: Exterior front-door glazing only, subject to measured fit. Keep internal clear-glass office/media door pairs uncovered in the gallery. High gallery glazing is reviewed separately for neighboring sightlines.
rooms.why: The two-story chandelier, arch and light doors should remain the focus. Full-height curtains add bulk; street-level entrance glass may still need evening privacy.
rooms.day: Entrance shade raised; gallery bright and open.
rooms.night: Lower the entrance privacy shade if the street can see into the house. Keep internal gallery doors visually clear.
rooms.installation: Provisional allowance for one compact door-mounted privacy solution; verify the arched glass, hardware, attachment and door swing. Do not cover inscriptions. Omit the purchase if the actual glass already provides adequate privacy.
rooms.title: Entrance gallery

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + hidden light-filtering privacy shades
rooms.coverage: Both main exterior banks are centered paired 2×2 groups, with TWO structural units in each bank. Preserve the small circular portico-side window and clear internal gallery doors; assess round-window privacy separately on site.
rooms.why: Adjustable glare control helps screen work and calls; a separate privacy layer lets you work after dark without closing the room off all day. Blackout is unnecessary for normal office use.
rooms.day: Sheers soften sun; adjust the shade on the bright side for monitor glare.
rooms.night: Lower privacy shades on both exterior window walls.
rooms.installation: Keep window access, full north-wall cabinetry, southeast desk/chair and door routes clear. Use a non-see-through privacy fabric, not an open solar screen; check it with interior lights on.
rooms.title: Home office

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout-lined curtains; removable clear-door covers for movie mode
rooms.coverage: One REAL centered paired 2×2 street-facing window, plus a separate removable opaque cover for each clear interior door leaf. The sofa wall is SOLID: its smaller exterior window feature is fake, as confirmed by the homeowner, and has no inside opening.
rooms.why: Daylight and gallery light both reduce contrast on the 83-inch TV. Privacy alone is insufficient for the requested theater atmosphere.
rooms.day: Sheers for casual use; close blackout panels for daytime films.
rooms.night: Close blackout panels and fit the room-side door covers for movies; dim lights near the screen.
rooms.installation: Resolve curtain overlap, returns and head gap. Use removable room-side covers with a finish-compatible attachment and storage location; each door must remain operable with handles clear. Keep figurine shelves and the west-wall doorway unobstructed. Allowance includes these covers; do not frost the doors permanently.
rooms.title: Media room

rooms.recommendation: Washable light-filtering privacy roller shades; no loose drapes
rooms.coverage: Large two-sash exterior window and smaller portico-side window; no curtains on the internal doors.
rooms.why: Shades control mirror glare and street privacy without loose fabric in future equipment space. Workout use does not require blackout.
rooms.day: Raise or partly lower shades to reduce mirror glare.
rooms.night: Lower privacy shades for exercise with the lights on.
rooms.installation: Choose cordless, wipeable material; keep northwest closet access, mirror and quote clear. Room remains unfurnished and equipment-free in this design.
rooms.title: Studio gym

rooms.recommendation: No window treatment
rooms.coverage: Bath #3 is windowless in the documented layout.
rooms.why: There is no exterior glazing to dress. Do not add a curtain allowance for a reflected or imagined opening.
rooms.day: Use planned task and ambient lighting.
rooms.night: Privacy comes from the bathroom door.
rooms.installation: Verify the existing room during survey; revise only if an actual exterior opening is found.
rooms.title: Bath #3

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + hidden privacy shades; no mandatory blackout
rooms.coverage: Terrace-facing glazing. Leave the two high horizontal transoms beside the fireplace bare unless glare or a neighboring sightline requires treatment.
rooms.why: This is a social room with a TV, so flexible glare control and evening privacy matter more than cinema-level darkness. The airy main-floor appearance stays intact.
rooms.day: Sheers diffuse sun; adjust the privacy shade where glare reaches the TV.
rooms.night: Close privacy shades when the room is visible from outside.
rooms.installation: Coordinate a traversing solution at operable terrace glass; stacks must clear handles and passage. Quote a blackout-fabric upgrade separately only if daytime TV testing shows it is wanted. High-transom treatment is not assumed in the base allowance.
rooms.title: Great room

rooms.recommendation: Wipeable privacy roller at the counter window
rooms.coverage: Kitchen counter window only. Adjacent sunroom window banks are counted in the sunroom.
rooms.why: The kitchen needs daylight and evening privacy, with a finish that tolerates cooking and cleaning. Full-length drapes are impractical at a counter or splash area.
rooms.day: Raise or partly lower for working light and glare control.
rooms.night: Lower the non-see-through privacy shade.
rooms.installation: Select washable material and a compact cordless mechanism; survey faucet, backsplash, handles and appliance clearances. No blackout required.
rooms.title: Kitchen

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + discreet privacy shades at tall windows
rooms.coverage: Four tall dining openings: two rectangular windows with shallow transoms on the east facade and two arched windows on the south facade. The smaller high-sill arch near the open living junction stays bare unless a sightline check requires coverage. Preserve the real butler-pantry passage; the oblique photo feature is not a proven closed niche.
rooms.why: Dinner after dark requires privacy while daytime entertaining benefits from light. Heavy blackout is unnecessary and should not obscure the arched architecture when open.
rooms.day: Sheers filter daylight; privacy layers fully raised and curtain stacks off glass.
rooms.night: Lower the privacy layer at all tall openings.
rooms.installation: Survey each opening individually. Mount the privacy layer to cover the whole tall opening, including an arch when closed, while clearing its shape when raised. Verify space above arches; price any required specialty arch treatment separately instead of assuming a standard roller fits.
rooms.title: Formal dining

rooms.recommendation: Clear ivory sheers + hidden privacy/glare shades
rooms.coverage: Two real tall windows on the east facade (printed-plan bottom/right), with matching sheers and privacy/glare shades. The north facade feature is a False Window and its interior face stays solid; no inside drape or shade there.
rooms.why: Maintain the bright piano salon and soft Cloud-style seating, with privacy after dark. An adjustable layer also helps reduce direct sun at the piano; sheers alone are not a complete sun-protection strategy.
rooms.day: Sheers drawn lightly; shade only where direct sun or glare calls for it.
rooms.night: Lower privacy shades on the front windows.
rooms.installation: Coordinate stack-back with piano lid, seating and circulation; confirm piano placement and environmental guidance with the chosen manufacturer. No blackout requirement.
rooms.title: Living room · piano salon

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + independent privacy shades by window bank
rooms.coverage: Wraparound lower glazing and terrace-door glass as measured. High transoms stay open visually unless an actual sightline or glare issue requires coverage.
rooms.why: The six-seat breakfast area should feel bright. Separate shades let you manage individual sunny sides and evening privacy without making the whole room dark.
rooms.day: Use sheers; lower only the shade on the sunniest side as needed.
rooms.night: Close the privacy layer where neighbors can see in.
rooms.installation: Split shade zones at real mullions and provide a compatible operable-door solution. Keep fabric and stacks clear of oven/cooking surfaces and door travel. Match the main-floor sheer color; no heavy blackout lining in the base.
rooms.title: Sunroom

rooms.recommendation: Bare high glazing by default; privacy review before ordering
rooms.coverage: Existing high stacked stair windows.
rooms.why: The landing and quarter-turn stair benefit from daylight; loose drapes would add clutter at circulation. No sleep or cinema use requires blackout.
rooms.day: Keep glass open visually; add fixed diffusion only if glare warrants it.
rooms.night: Check views from neighboring upper floors; height alone does not guarantee privacy.
rooms.installation: No new covering in the base budget. If the survey reveals a sightline, price a discreet privacy treatment and safe operating/cleaning access separately. Keep fabric away from treads and guards.
rooms.title: Second-floor stair hall

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + fully closing oatmeal blackout-lined curtains
rooms.coverage: Full four-sash rear window group. Coordinate the open retreat as part of the same sleep-darkening zone.
rooms.why: The primary bedroom needs sleeping darkness, daytime rest and evening privacy. Treating only this room would leave light entering through the open retreat.
rooms.day: Sheers filter daylight; blackout layer stacks clear.
rooms.night: Close both bedroom and retreat blackout layers; switch off decorative under-bed lighting for sleep if preferred.
rooms.installation: Use independent tracks with overlap/returns. Check the dresser below the window before deciding curtain drop and stack. If it prevents full closure, use a blackout roller behind the sheers rather than trapping fabric behind furniture. Inspect all light gaps after installation.
rooms.title: Owners suite

rooms.recommendation: Match the bedroom: ivory sheers + blackout layer
rooms.coverage: Both exterior window walls and any connected terrace-door glazing confirmed on site. Do not add a door to the open bedroom connection.
rooms.why: Although this is a sitting/coffee area, it is open to the bedroom. Untreated retreat glass would defeat the bedroom blackout treatment.
rooms.day: Sheers for the lounge; blackout curtains stacked away from glass.
rooms.night: Close all retreat exterior-glass blackout layers with the bedroom curtains.
rooms.installation: Survey all window groups and terrace access. Keep curtains clear of the bar, appliances and door swings. Where a door cannot accept curtains, use an independent blackout shade with gap control; keep the visible fabric coordinated with the bedroom.
rooms.title: Owners retreat

rooms.recommendation: Wet-area privacy at shower glass; moisture-resistant shade at dry window
rooms.coverage: Exterior window within the shower and the dry vanity-side exterior window.
rooms.why: Bathing needs reliable privacy, not decorative sheers. Fabric in direct shower spray is unsuitable; bedroom blackout can be managed with the bathroom door closed.
rooms.day: Shower-window privacy remains in place while admitting diffuse daylight; adjust the dry-window shade.
rooms.night: Close the dry-window opaque privacy shade; verify the shower treatment conceals silhouettes under actual interior lighting.
rooms.installation: Provisional base: obscuring film explicitly compatible with the shower exposure and existing glazing, plus a moisture-resistant opaque roller on the dry window. If film cannot meet privacy/compatibility needs, quote suitable obscured glazing separately; window replacement is not included. No hanging sheer or drape in the shower.
rooms.title: Owners bathroom

rooms.recommendation: No window treatment
rooms.coverage: Windowless closet in the current plan-led concept.
rooms.why: No exterior opening needs a covering; preserve storage and task lighting.
rooms.day: Use closet lighting.
rooms.night: Privacy is provided by the suite and closet enclosure.
rooms.installation: Confirm during measured survey; do not invent a window to match a render reflection.
rooms.title: Owners walk-in closet

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout-lined curtains or concealed blackout roller
rooms.coverage: Wide front window on plan-bottom wall and narrow side window on plan-right wall. Headboard on stair-hall wall (plan-top); closet on shared-bathroom boundary (plan-left).
rooms.why: A sleeping room needs darkness and nighttime privacy even when also used for study. The desk is not a reason to omit blackout.
rooms.day: Sheers and an adjustable shade position for study light.
rooms.night: Fully close the blackout layer.
rooms.installation: Keep desk access and window operation clear. Prefer full closing curtains where they fit; if the desk blocks their travel, use a blackout roller with suitable edge overlap behind the sheers. No freestanding furniture changes required.
rooms.title: Bedroom 2

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout at every exterior opening
rooms.coverage: Large front window and both smaller windows flanking the bed.
rooms.why: All three openings must darken for comfortable sleeping; dressing only the large window would leave the bedside windows admitting light.
rooms.day: Sheers preserve a light guest-bedroom atmosphere.
rooms.night: Close all three blackout layers.
rooms.installation: Use functional lined curtains where stack space allows and matching discreet blackout rollers behind sheers at tight bedside openings. Check bedside furniture, wall lights and bedding clearance before fixing tracks.
rooms.title: Bedroom 3

rooms.recommendation: No window treatment
rooms.coverage: No exterior window in this bathroom; bedroom glazing seen through doors or mirrors belongs to the bedrooms.
rooms.why: Bathroom privacy comes from closing its doors. Avoid ordering shades for reflected windows.
rooms.day: Use planned bathroom lighting.
rooms.night: Close bathroom doors; adjacent bedroom coverings are priced in those rooms.
rooms.installation: Confirm the windowless condition in the site survey.
rooms.title: Shared bathroom

rooms.recommendation: Washable privacy rollers; lined woven-look shades as an alternative
rooms.coverage: Two left-side windows, including the arched opening by the sink.
rooms.why: Laundry needs useful daylight, washable finishes and evening privacy. Open-weave decorative shades alone may be see-through; blackout and floor-length curtains are unnecessary.
rooms.day: Raise for task light; adjust to soften glare.
rooms.night: Lower the privacy layer.
rooms.installation: Survey the arch and sink clearance; cover the full sightline without hanging fabric into splashes. If a woven-look Roman shade is chosen instead, include a privacy lining in its quote. Preserve the Rinse and repeat.. graphic.
rooms.title: Laundry

rooms.recommendation: Bare high windows; add privacy only if sightlines require it
rooms.coverage: Three high stair-hall windows.
rooms.why: Daylight supports circulation; the stair does not need blackout or floor-length fabric.
rooms.day: Leave glass visually open; assess glare on the landing.
rooms.night: Check neighboring upper-floor views before treating high glazing as private.
rooms.installation: No covering included in base. Survey any needed discreet privacy/diffusion treatment and access cost separately; do not hang fabric into stair travel or against the guard.
rooms.title: Third-floor stair hall

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + independent privacy layers at terrace glazing
rooms.coverage: French doors and flanking windows, wide terrace slider and compact bar-alcove window. Coordinate the final glazing inventory on site.
rooms.why: The penthouse lounge should retain its views by day and privacy after dark. Being on the top floor does not guarantee privacy from adjacent homes. It is not currently a sleeping room or dedicated cinema.
rooms.day: Sheers for soft light; raise the compact bar-window shade.
rooms.night: Close privacy layers where visible from neighboring properties.
rooms.installation: Use traversing treatments that stack clear of the slider and French doors; compact shade at the bar. Blackout is a separate future upgrade if this becomes a regular sleeping or cinema space. Interior loft glass is not also counted in terrace furniture costs.
rooms.title: Penthouse lounge

rooms.recommendation: Ivory sheers + blackout for the new guest bedroom
rooms.coverage: Confirmed exterior glazing of the proposed new Bedroom 5 only; openings and final enclosure remain to be surveyed.
rooms.why: This is a real sleeping room, so guest privacy and light control should be designed into construction rather than added after furniture arrives.
rooms.day: Sheers filter daylight.
rooms.night: Close the blackout layer at every confirmed exterior opening.
rooms.installation: Provisional allowance, not an approved window count. Coordinate track supports and bed/storage positions with the new room plan. Do not create new windows or drape the blank headboard wall to imitate a render.
rooms.title: Penthouse guest bedroom

rooms.recommendation: No window treatment in the current layout
rooms.coverage: Plan-led penthouse bathroom is windowless.
rooms.why: No exterior glazing needs dressing in the documented concept.
rooms.day: Use bathroom lighting.
rooms.night: Use the bathroom door for privacy.
rooms.installation: Confirm the existing enclosure/services and whether there is any real exterior opening before final scope. A newly discovered window would require a wet-area privacy specification and revised allowance.
rooms.title: Penthouse bathroom

rooms.recommendation: No interior drapes outdoors
rooms.coverage: Outdoor roof terrace; adjoining interior glass is covered under the loft or suite room schedule.
rooms.why: Interior sheers and blackout panels do not belong in this outdoor exposure. Existing exterior shade structures and weather-rated furniture form a separate scope.
rooms.day: Use the existing outdoor shade arrangement.
rooms.night: Close the relevant interior privacy layers from inside.
rooms.installation: No additional exterior curtain system included; do not duplicate loft glazing costs here.
rooms.title: Roof terrace
